title: the inference proxy keeps its answers in a tree and its meter in the log
intention: The inference proxy's stored answers live in a tree it holds by the librarian's delegation (outline 13.3.4.1, 4.3.1.6), its meter (yield and calls) reads the inference tickets in the logs tree, and the inference_calls table that did both jobs is retired with every stored answer carried into the tree.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: inference_calls (owner inference_domain, domain.py:96) does two jobs. 11,395 'miss' rows (11,366 distinct requests) carry the stored answers resolve() serves from (_latest_valid_answer, domain.py:453); 9,416 'hit' and 58 'refused' rows are meter only. yield_report (domain.py:777) and the calls verb (device.py:62) read every row. The logs tree already holds every call as an inference ticket with verdict and cost (11,942 files under ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets, written by _write_task_ticket, domain.py:305). The librarian separately copies answers into its nodes (librarian/ingest.py, 250 so far), so answers are kept twice and the meter twice. Akien 2026-11-05 (outline 4.3.1.8): 'it's saying anything we're going to store LEARNING in database memory'; on inference_calls: 'that's a file in the logging tree i think? or did you mean the learning blocks inside of the inference proxy?'; on the split into a tree for answers and the log for the meter: 'yes i think so'.
traces_to: Law 1 (a compiled answer is learning and belongs where the librarian can see it), outline 4.3.1.8 and 13.3.4.1 (Akien 2026-11-05), Law 5 (one home per thing), RULE 1 (inference_domain's own code; the trees tool through its public interface).
how: resolve() stores each new answer through the librarian's published trees tool into a leaf table the proxy owns, inference_domain_answers_nodes, and looks a request up there by its canonical form (exact, via the request's content-hash node id), keeping today's horizon check. yield_report and the calls verb read the inference tickets in the logs tree, same output keys as today. New one-shot cairn/devices/inference_domain/migrate_answers_to_their_tree.py: for each distinct canonical among miss rows, carry its latest still-valid answer into the tree, compare the carried set with the distinct-canonical set, and only on a match (after pg_dump -t inference_calls to ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/temp/) drop inference_calls; exit non-zero on any mismatch. The answers to open-029c5ae100a9 (vectors) and open-c9e699e669e2 (all-time yield) fix the leaf's shape and where the yield total lives; the build waits on them.
falsifier: (1) no non-proof module under cairn/devices/inference_domain names inference_calls; (2) in a scratch answer tree, resolve() of a new request with a counting fake resolver stores its answer, and a second identical resolve() returns the same answer with verdict 'hit' and the resolver still called once; (3) a stored answer past its horizon is not served and the resolver is called again; (4) yield_report over a scratch logs tree of known tickets returns exactly their hit/miss/refused counts and their spent/avoided sums; (5) the calls verb over a scratch logs tree returns tickets newest first, bounded by limit, carrying the keys librarian/ingest.py reads; (6) the migration over a scratch table of miss, hit, refused and expired rows carries one answer per distinct canonical, a second run writes nothing, and a forced mismatch drops nothing and exits non-zero; (7) live, read-only, after the migration has run: inference_calls does not exist, store.owner_of('inference_domain_answers_nodes') is 'inference_domain', its leaf count is at least 11,366, and the pg_dump file exists; (8) median lookup time over 100 scratch tree lookups is recorded beside the median of today's table read, and the tree's is no more than 3x; (9) every proof under cairn/devices/inference_domain stays green.

out: cairn/devices/librarian/ingest.py (the librarian's own follow-up: its copy of the answers becomes redundant)
the logs tree's 30-day sweep (not running: oldest ticket 2026-09-17)

decisions.text: D1 (the /sorted builder_check): A Haiku builder needs: the owner and table name (inference_domain, inference_domain_answers_nodes), the trees tool's public functions to use (ensure_trees, deposit, a lookup by node id), that the horizon check moves with the answer, the log ticket path and keys, the migration's verify-before-drop rule with the pg_dump path, the proof path with one tooth per clause; and the two answers (vectors, yield total), which are opened as questions and hold BUILDME.
